reviews.summary: "on the morning" is ungrammatical in the lead, the first thing the reader sees.; "Show your working" is British school slang (US says "show your work"). VOICE.md says lines must work for US and UK readers, and this is a line people will copy.; "the same film" has nothing to be the same as, so the joke doesn't land. The Spanish ("la misma película de siempre") gets it right.

dealbreakers: The Snow Globe note (EN and ES) describes the template wrongly. It says to write 'two to four short lines' that make up the message, that 'the closing words' get engraved, and that 'the whole message' then opens. In the code, at most four reveals appear (shakes: two/three/four), they alternate line and photo, and the template needs at least one photo, so four lines can never all appear. With two or more photos, only two lines show (storm.ts revealPlan, Template.tsx line 101, manifest photos.min 1). The plaque is a separate field of up to 44 characters, or the gift's title if left empty (schema.ts plaque, Template.tsx line 189). What opens at the end is the gift's main message (data.message), not the lines (Template.tsx Letter).
reviews.summary: Factual error: four lines can't all appear alongside photos, the plaque is its own field, and the letter holds the main message. The old opening also echoed the girlfriend post's 'For a message told in pieces'.; Same factual error. 'en dos a cuatro frases' is also not natural Spanish.; The photos hang on a string below the letter, after it, not beside it (fireside/Template.tsx Reading). 'For a quieter one' echoes the girlfriend post's 'For a quieter Christmas message'.; Same correction as the English (photos hang below, not beside).; Near-verbatim copy of the christmas-letter-to-mom note: 'a sealed envelope, your words in a handwriting font, and a few photos at the end.'; Matches the English

In a results list, "Eve to night" reads like a typo for "Eve tonight". "Bedtime" says the same thing clearly (53 chars, inside the 20–60 test).; Nochebuena is already a night, so "de Nochebuena a la noche" doesn't make sense as a span. "Al 25" matches the post (54 chars).; "On the morning" is ungrammatical, and it's in the lead that Google shows as the snippet.; "Short" is the most common modifier people add to this search, and every top listicle uses it. It also matches the girlfriend post's heading pattern.; Spanish searchers type "frases ... cortas". This keeps EN and ES aligned.
